subject: Urgent: production model-serving degradation impacting Clearline Financial - executive support requested
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@clearline.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: ops-support@clearline.com
Date: 2026-10-07T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production degradation — sustained 500s + high tail latency (Clearline Reserved)

Irene,

We started seeing a significant uptick in 5xx errors and long tail latencies on our payment reconciliation endpoint at ~07:50 PT. This is on our reserved capacity (contract DL-4498) — the traffic profile is normal for us (no unusual spike on our side).

Impact: multiple customer jobs failing (retries bumping QPS), downstream settlement delays, and a rising error rate that has triggered our incident playbook. Our SREs are seeing requests queueing for >2.5s and a ~12% 500 rate in the last 10 minutes.

Please confirm receipt and proposed immediate mitigations. We need an ETA for a fix (or an acceptable workaround) and whether Redwood can authorize a burst or fallback while you investigate. If exec-level help is needed, we expect Redwood to loop in the necessary leadership.

Attached: support_log_snapshot_2026-10-07.txt (truncated).

— Maria
Maria Gomez
SRE Lead, Clearline Financial
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@clearline.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, dylan.brooks@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-07T08:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production degradation — sustained 500s + high tail latency (Clearline Reserved)

Maria —

Thank you for the alert and the log snapshot. I’m escalating this immediately. Short summary of immediate steps we’re initiating:
- Dylan (SRE) is triaging root cause and will post findings within 15-20 minutes.
- We are preparing a temporary fallback plan: enable burst capacity for DL-4498 and open a limited failover route to the compatible smaller model for non-critical reconciliation jobs (if you approve).
- I’ve looped in Marissa (your account lead) for compensation/contract alignment and Vivek for any cross-team authorizations required for a one-time burst.

Maria, can you confirm if you want us to start toggling the fallback path while we triage? We will only route lower-priority background jobs to the smaller model unless you ask otherwise.

I will follow up with the triage notes.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@clearline.com>, ops-support@clearline.com
Date: 2026-10-07T08:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production degradation — triage notes + immediate mitigations

Team / Maria —

Quick triage (observed):
- Dedicated GPU pool serving DL-4498 shows sustained 100% vGPU utilization across 5 nodes for the last 18 minutes.
- KV cache growth for the deployed model jumped (cache miss ratio fell) — suspected working set expansion from longer context windows in a subset of customer jobs.
- Autoscaling attempted to add capacity but hit reserved pool ceiling (the Dedicated pool assigned to DL-4498 is saturated).
- Result: request queueing at the front-end, token-generation time increases -> 500-rate increases due to timeouts in our proxy (we have conservative proxy timeouts for reconciliation jobs).

Immediate mitigations we can do now (impact/risk):
1) Enable one-time burst (hot spare capacity) for 60m — requires exec approval for overage. This will relieve queueing immediately. (LOW risk)
2) Evict largest KV entries and reduce max_context for the model instance (risk: increased token-cost / minor quality delta) — we can do this in a rolling fashion. (MEDIUM risk)
3) Route background reconciliation workers to a smaller quantized variant we host (throughput-friendly) — requires Clearline sign-off for any non-critical jobs. (LOW risk to core requests)
4) Apply temporary rate-limit on extremely long-running requests (>4s) to prevent cascade of queueing. (LOW risk, customer-visible for some edge jobs)

Attached are the short log snapshot and the latency charts (latency_charts_20261007.pdf).

I recommend we 1) get burst approved from leadership now, 2) immediately enable fallback routing for non-critical jobs, and 3) start cache eviction and reduced context rollouts. Jonas — can you flag capacity/finance implications for the burst? Vivek — please confirm approval for burst overage so SREs can toggle.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@clearline.com>, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-07T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production degradation — Clearline reserved capacity (commercial path)

Maria —

I’m sorry you’re seeing this. From a commercial/CS perspective we’ll do the following once SRE confirms the technical mitigation:
- Approve a one-time buffer credit to offset any immediate overage generated by a burst authorization (I’ll prepare the credit memo now).
- If the root cause is an under-sized reservation, we will expedite a revised commitment path (short-term uplift + evaluation period) so you don’t encounter repeated saturation.

For the burst approval: Vivek / Jonas — we need a rapid sign-off for a 60-minute hot-spare burst while Dylan and SREs execute the fallback. The ask is to briefly exceed the reserved throughput at the committed price (we’ll record the overage and apply the credit). Please confirm so we can move.

Maria — if agreeable, Marissa here can open the temporary failover for lower-priority jobs within 5 minutes of sign-off.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai, dylan.brooks@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-07T09:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production degradation — approval for hot-spare burst

Approved: authorize 60-minute hot-spare burst for DL-4498 now.
Notes:
- Finance: Jonas, capture the overage as a billable event then apply the one-time credit retroactively (Marissa to prepare).
- Ops: Dylan, proceed with enabling the fallback routing for non-critical jobs and start cache eviction. Keep Maria updated every 10 minutes.
- Post-mortem: schedule a joint incident post-mortem and capacity planning session by EOD tomorrow; engineering + account team + Clearline.

Irene — please send a short customer-facing update once the burst is live and we see the first signs of degradation abating.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Engineering (acting CTO)
Redwood Inference
